intro: This week saw rapid advances in large‑language models, new benchmarks exposing multimodal gaps, and strategic moves in AI hardware and governance.

articles.headline: Anthropic rolls out Claude Haiku 5.5, a faster low‑cost LLM
articles.summary: Anthropic introduced Claude Haiku 5.5, replacing the 4.5 version with a token throughput of 237 t/s and improved benchmark scores while maintaining its low per‑token pricing. The model targets developers needing high‑speed inference for simple tasks such as summarisation and classification, expanding the portfolio of affordable LLM options.
articles.why_it_matters: A cheaper, high‑throughput model lowers barriers for small‑scale developers and broadens the ecosystem of cost‑effective AI services.

articles.headline: Claude Sonnet 5.5 adds adaptive reasoning for code‑centric agents
articles.summary: Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5.5 arrives with adaptive reasoning levels, enhanced tool‑use capabilities, and top placement on Artificial Analysis’s Coding Agent Index. While higher reasoning tiers cost more per task, the model sets a new performance baseline for routine coding and office‑automation agents.
articles.why_it_matters: It demonstrates the trade‑off between cost and accuracy that developers must manage when deploying LLM‑powered agents for productivity tasks.

articles.headline: Mistral Large 4 ("le Chonk") leads European open‑weight LLMs for security work
articles.summary: Mistral unveiled Large 4, a 1.05 trillion‑parameter mixture‑of‑experts model supporting up to 1 M tokens. In the CyberGym‑E2E benchmark it achieved an 82 % score, the highest among publicly available models, and is positioned as Europe’s strategic asset for cybersecurity workloads.
articles.why_it_matters: The model strengthens European AI sovereignty in a critical domain, offering a home‑grown alternative to dominant US and Chinese offerings.

articles.headline: NVIDIA launches DGX Spark desktop for on‑premise AI agents
articles.summary: NVIDIA announced the DGX Spark, a desktop‑sized system delivering 1 petaflop of compute power. Designed for fine‑tuning and inference of local AI agents, the platform aims to reduce dependence on cloud resources for edge AI workloads.
articles.why_it_matters: Providing petaflop‑class compute at the desk level enables developers to experiment with large models locally, accelerating prototyping and improving data‑privacy control.

articles.headline: Humanity’s Sixth Sense benchmark highlights multimodal reasoning gap
articles.summary: Elorian and Scale AI released the HSS benchmark, comprising 522 image and video questions that test temporal, spatial, social and abstract reasoning. Humans achieve ~93 % pass@1, while GPT‑6 Astra scores 53.6 % and Chinese open‑weight models fall below 27 %.
articles.why_it_matters: The results underline persistent shortcomings in visual‑reasoning AI, informing safety assessments and future research priorities for multimodal systems.

articles.headline: TasteVal benchmark shows AI research creativity accelerating
articles.summary: P‑Zero Research’s TasteVal evaluates models on eight frontier‑AI tasks, finding that experimental research taste has doubled roughly every three months since December 2025. Opus 5.5 outperforms human experts with about 2.3× compute efficiency.
articles.why_it_matters: Rapid gains in AI’s ability to select and design research problems suggest progress toward recursive self‑improvement, a key milestone for advanced AI systems.

articles.headline: US national labs demonstrate federated training of LLaMA‑based models
articles.summary: Sandia, LLNL and LANL jointly trained LLaMA 3.x models up to 70 B parameters using AMD MI300A and NVIDIA H100 GPUs, employing federated frameworks (NVFlare, Flower, APPFL) to keep classified data on‑site while scaling compute across three facilities.
articles.why_it_matters: The effort shows a viable path for secure, collaborative AI development within government, setting a precedent for future large‑scale, classified model training.
